NODE_PATH points at /usr/local/lib/node_modules_global and /opt/node-tools tools are resolvable, which silently changes the output of resolution-based JS tools like depcheck (eslint/typescript 'used' in 15 packages); worth a line for benchmark runs: clear NODE_PATH.

deviations.did: Added --deps to cyclehound with a depcheck-exact mode and a measured comparison.

deviations.why: Running depcheck on third-party npm tarballs with default specials would require() their config files (executing their code).
deviations.did: Ran depcheck with only its bin and react17 specials on the npm corpus; defaults on this repo.
deviations.result: Comparison stayed safe; the scope is stated in BENCHMARK.md.

goal: dev tools in Rust: one binary for cycles, unused exports and dependency hygiene
notes: Idea: cyclehound --deps, depcheck in Rust on the existing lexer. --depcheck matches depcheck 1.4.7 on 32 repo packages and 442 npm-tarball packages (9 names explained by depcheck parse failures). Five undocumented depcheck behaviours reproduced (relative import -> '.' -> own peers used; self-reference via exports; parenthesised strings; URL drop only for import/require; type-position import() skipped). Found and fixed a lexer bug (o.else / e read as regex). Default mode: 81 -> 4 findings on this repo, all real (esbuild and @eslint/eslintrc in ai-first-markets, @lexical/history in report-app, vite undeclared in local-site-studio); not removed (lockfile edits belong to those ventures). Local verification: cargo test 36 pass, clippy -D warnings and fmt clean, node --test 21 pass, check_posts ok. Next: measure depcheck-rs; Vue/Svelte script blocks; --deps in the wasm page.

certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured
